title: Private: Repair header aliasing + KMS fallback to stop silent audit suppression during rolling upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise Private customers reported missing audit events correlated with SAML-driven role changes during an on-prem rolling upgrade window. Investigation traced the gap to a short-lived mismatch between the tenant encryption header alias used by the control-plane proxy and the KMS envelope metadata expected by the audit writer. In affected requests the audit writer treated the request as 'unencrypted' and suppressed tenant-identifying audit fields, resulting in silent/partial audit entries for ~2026-03-12 02:00Z -> 2026-03-13 10:00Z on several clusters.

How it reproduces (internal steps):
1) Configure a Private cluster with SAML SSO and KMS envelope wrapping enabled.
2) Trigger a rolling upgrade of control-plane proxies while performing SAML role-change flows with RelayState > 200 bytes.
3) Observe that proxy rewrites a long header (X-Redwood-Tenant-Encrypt) into a shorter alias (X-RW-T-Enc) during chunked transfer under load.
4) Audit writer failed to map the alias to the active KMS key id because the envelope's key-id metadata used a fully-qualified identifier; the alias path led to a lookup miss and an implicit fallback path that intentionally suppresses tenant fields pending successful decrypt.

Root cause: A combination of header aliasing by the proxy (introduced in the rolling upgrade) and a strict KMS envelope key-id normalization check in the audit writer produced a transient key-id lookup miss. The audit writer code path was designed to avoid blocking writes on decrypt failures and therefore suppressed tenant-identifying fields rather than failing the request or emitting an explicit audit error. This design decision caused missing/partial audit events rather than loud failures.

Scope: Affects Private clusters that met all three conditions: (1) KMS envelope wrapping enabled, (2) SAML flows with long RelayState causing header aliasing under current proxy code-path, (3) rolling upgrade timeframe where proxy header behavior and control-plane key metadata could be briefly inconsistent. We have confirmed 6 customer clusters with partial missing events; broad impact limited by these preconditions.

Immediate mitigation (hotfix):
- Accept header aliases in the audit writer: accept both X-Redwood-Tenant-Encrypt and X-RW-T-Enc and normalize before key-id lookup.
- Add a KMS fallback path that checks cached previous key versions and envelope signature header (X-Redwood-Encrypt-Sig) before suppressing tenant fields.
- Emit an explicit audit-error event when decrypt lookup fails so operators can alert rather than silently lose tenant data.

Planned permanent fix:
1) Patch control-plane proxy to preserve canonical header names for encryption metadata during upgrades (short-term compatibility shim).
2) Update audit writer to normalize header aliases and perform robust key canonicalization (accept numeric and fqid forms).
3) Add conservative audit-mode toggle: for hotfix deploys we will temporarily fail writes loudly (fail-open=false) and call operator pager for any decrypt metadata lookup failures for a 48-hour window after deploy.
4) Add reconciliation job that scans write-ahead logs and replays/generates reconstructed audit entries for the affected time window, using cached envelopes and transport logs to rehydrate tenant ids where safe.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for header alias normalization and key-id canonicalization.
- Integration tests simulating rolling upgrade + long RelayState requests to validate aliasing path.
- Staging run: deploy hotfix to one non-prod Private cluster with synthetic SSO flows and verify no audit suppression.
- Canary: deploy to two affected customer clusters with feature-flagged fail-open=false and on-call watch.

Rollback plan:
- Hotfix will be feature-flagged. Rollback by reverting feature flag to previous behavior.
- If reconciliation job introduces any unintended data duplication, stop job and revert to snapshot before replay.

Operator runbook (high level):
- If customers report missing audit events: check cluster flight logs for header alias pattern, check audit-writer logs for 'decrypt-lookup-miss' marker, escalate to on-call.
- To force reconciliation for a specific cluster: run: /ops/replay-audit --cluster <id> --from 2026-03-12T02:00Z --to 2026-03-13T10:00Z (internal tool).

Customer comms:
- Draft apology + mitigation note ready (link to Confluence incident summary). We have communicated to impacted customers and committed to a reconciliation window and follow-up verification.

Links & artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8123 (hotfix branch)
- Staging results: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/upgrade/audit-replay-staging
- Incident writeup (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/2026-03-12+Private+Audit+Suppression+Investigation
- Customer tickets: CUST-8342, CUST-8347, CUST-8399

Notes / trade-offs:
- We deliberately avoid long-term fail-open behavior; the immediate hotfix will surface failures to avoid silent data loss. This may cause brief customer-visible errors during the 48-hour hard-fail window and will require tight on-call staffing.
- Reconciliation relies on cached envelope metadata; in rare cases where cached material is evicted we will need customer-assisted revalidation (out-of-band).
